name: 1x2 Beam
use: A 1x2 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 2 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 2x Pitch Shaft
use: A 2x pitch shaft is a square metal axle 2 holes long. It carries rotation from a motor to gears, wheels, and sprockets, which lock onto its square shape. Hold it in place with rubber shaft collars, and let it spin freely through round holes in beams.

name: 1x4 Beam
use: A 1x4 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 4 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 4x Pitch Shaft
use: A 4x pitch shaft is a square metal axle 4 holes long. It carries rotation from a motor to gears, wheels, and sprockets, which lock onto its square shape. Hold it in place with rubber shaft collars, and let it spin freely through round holes in beams.

name: 1x6 Beam
use: A 1x6 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 6 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 6x Pitch Shaft
use: A 6x pitch shaft is a square metal axle 6 holes long. It carries rotation from a motor to gears, wheels, and sprockets, which lock onto its square shape. Hold it in place with rubber shaft collars, and let it spin freely through round holes in beams.

name: 1x8 Beam
use: A 1x8 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 8 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 8x Pitch Shaft
use: A 8x pitch shaft is a square metal axle 8 holes long. It carries rotation from a motor to gears, wheels, and sprockets, which lock onto its square shape. Hold it in place with rubber shaft collars, and let it spin freely through round holes in beams.

name: 1x10 Beam
use: A 1x10 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 10 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 2x10 Beam
use: A 2x10 beam is a double-wide beam (10 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x2 Beam
use: A 2x2 beam is a small square block of four holes used to join two beams side by side, add a mounting point, or build compact brackets. Connect it with connector pins.

name: 2x4 Beam
use: A 2x4 beam is a double-wide beam (4 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x6 Beam
use: A 2x6 beam is a double-wide beam (6 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x7 Beam
use: A 2x7 beam is a double-wide beam (7 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x8 Beam
use: A 2x8 beam is a double-wide beam (8 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x8 Smooth Panel
use: The smooth panel is a flat piece with a smooth surface, used for walls, scoops, ramps, and guides where game pieces need to slide without catching on holes.

name: 2x3 Right Angle Beam
use: A right angle beam is bent at 90° to make L-shaped corners, brackets, and arms without needing a separate corner connector.

name: 3x4 Tee Beam
use: A tee beam is T-shaped, used to join three directions at once, such as a cross-brace or the top of a support tower.

name: 3x5 Right Angle Beam
use: A right angle beam is bent at 90° to make L-shaped corners, brackets, and arms without needing a separate corner connector.

name: 4x4 Offset Right Angle Beam
use: An offset right angle beam is an L-shaped beam whose arms are shifted, useful for brackets and arms that need to step around another part.

name: 3x3 30 Degree Angle Beam
use: A 30° angle beam is bent at 30° for building slanted arms, ramps, and triangle braces that make a structure stronger.

name: 3x3 45 Degree Angle Beam
use: A 45° angle beam is bent at 45° for building slanted arms, ramps, and triangle braces that make a structure stronger.

name: 3x3 60 Degree Angle Beam
use: A 60° angle beam is bent at 60° for building slanted arms, ramps, and triangle braces that make a structure stronger.

name: 3x3 Plus Gusset Beam
use: A plus gusset beam is a cross (+) shaped piece used to join beams coming from four directions or to brace a joint so it doesn't flex.

name: Washer
use: A washer is a thin ring that slides onto a shaft between a spinning part and a beam. It reduces rubbing (friction) and adds a tiny bit of spacing so parts turn smoothly.

name: Rubber Shaft Collar
use: A rubber shaft collar grips a shaft tightly to keep it from sliding out of a build and to hold gears, wheels, and spacers in place along the shaft. Slide one on each end of a shaft.

name: 1x1 Connector Pin
use: The 1x1 connector pin is the most common way to join two parts: push it through one hole in each piece to lock two single-thickness parts together.

name: 1x2 Connector Pin
use: A 1x2 connector pin joins one part on one side to two stacked parts on the other side, for example a beam to a pair of beams.

name: 2x2 Connector Pin
use: A 2x2 connector pin joins two stacked parts on one side to two stacked parts on the other, making a strong, thick connection.

name: Large Chassis Corner Connector
use: The large chassis corner connector joins beams at the corners of a robot base (chassis), making a strong, square frame.

name: Small Chassis Corner Connector
use: The small chassis corner connector joins beams at the corners of a smaller frame or chassis, keeping it square and rigid.

name: 1x Wide, 1x1 Offset Corner Connector
use: The 1x Wide, 1x1 Offset Corner Connector joins single-width (1x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers. Offset versions shift where the connected part sits, which helps line up parts that would otherwise be one hole off.

name: 2x Wide, 1x2 Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 1x2 Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers.

name: 2x Wide, 1x2 Offset Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 1x2 Offset Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers. Offset versions shift where the connected part sits, which helps line up parts that would otherwise be one hole off.

name: 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers.

name: 1x Wide, 1x1 Corner Connector
use: The 1x Wide, 1x1 Corner Connector joins single-width (1x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers.

name: 2x Wide, 1x1 Offset Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 1x1 Offset Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers. Offset versions shift where the connected part sits, which helps line up parts that would otherwise be one hole off.

name: 2x Wide, 2x1 Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 2x1 Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers.

name: 2x Wide, 2x1 Offset Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 2x1 Offset Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers. Offset versions shift where the connected part sits, which helps line up parts that would otherwise be one hole off.

name: 2x Wide, 2x2 Offset Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 2x2 Offset Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers. Offset versions shift where the connected part sits, which helps line up parts that would otherwise be one hole off.

name: 2x Wide, 3x2 Corner Connector
use: The 2x Wide, 3x2 Corner Connector joins double-wide (2x) beams and plates at a 90° angle to build boxes, frames, and towers.

name: 2x Wide, 60 Degree Omni 1x2 Corner Connector
use: This corner connector joins parts at a 60° angle instead of 90°, for building slanted frames, triangle supports, and angled arms.

name: 90 Degree Standoff Connector
use: A 90° standoff connector joins standoffs or beams at a right angle, letting a structure turn a corner.

name: Double 2x Wide, 1x2 Corner Connector
use: The Double 2x Wide, 1x2 Corner Connector connects beams or plates on two sides at 90° angles, making strong box corners for chassis and towers in one piece.

name: Double 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector
use: The Double 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector connects beams or plates on two sides at 90° angles, making strong box corners for chassis and towers in one piece.

name: Double 2x Wide, 2x2 Double Offset Corner Connector
use: The Double 2x Wide, 2x2 Double Offset Corner Connector connects beams or plates on two sides at 90° angles, making strong box corners for chassis and towers in one piece.

name: Triple 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector
use: The Triple 2x Wide, 2x2 Corner Connector connects beams or plates on three sides at 90° angles, making strong box corners for chassis and towers in one piece.

name: Mini Standoff Connector
use: A mini standoff connector is a small connector for attaching standoffs to beams or to each other in tight spaces.

name: End Standoff Connector
use: An end standoff connector attaches to the end of a standoff so another part can be connected there, capping off or extending a standoff structure.

name: Medium Intake Flap
use: A medium intake flap attaches to a chain to build an intake or conveyor that grabs and pulls in larger game pieces.

name: Short Intake Flap
use: An intake flap attaches to a chain to build an intake or conveyor that grabs and pulls in game pieces.

name: Traction Link
use: Traction links snap into a chain to make a rubbery tank tread or conveyor belt surface that grips the ground or game pieces.

name: 1x Wide Spool
use: A spool winds up rope when it turns, making a winch to pull something up, like a lift or a drawbridge.

name: 24x Pitch Rope
use: The rope winds onto a spool to make a winch, pulling arms and lifts up or holding things in place.

name: Cable Anchor
use: A cable anchor holds Smart Cables against the robot so they don't snag on moving parts or get pulled out.

name: Rubber Band Anchor
use: A rubber band anchor gives a rubber band a place to hook onto a beam, so the band can pull an arm back, hold a claw closed, or help a lift.

name: Silicone Rubber Band #32
use: Rubber bands add spring force: they pull parts back to a position, keep claws closed, or help a motor lift an arm.

name: North Pole Magnetic Beam
use: A magnetic beam has a magnet built in. The north pole beam attracts the south pole beam, so they can be used for magnetic latches, grabbers, or parts that snap together and release.

name: South Pole Magnetic Beam
use: A magnetic beam has a magnet built in. The south pole beam attracts the north pole beam, so they can be used for magnetic latches, grabbers, or parts that snap together and release.

name: 1x12 Beam
use: A 1x12 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 12 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 2x12 Beam
use: A 2x12 beam is a double-wide beam (12 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 1x16 Beam
use: A 1x16 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 16 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 2x16 Beam
use: A 2x16 beam is a double-wide beam (16 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 3x3 Plate
use: A 3x3 plate is a small flat piece used as a base, a cover, or to brace a frame so it doesn't bend. Pins connect it to beams and connectors.

name: 4x4 Plate
use: A 4x4 plate is a flat square piece used as a base, a mounting surface, or to stiffen a frame. Pins connect it to beams and connectors.

name: 4x12 Plate
use: A 4x12 plate is a long flat piece used as a robot base or platform, or to make a wide, rigid surface.

name: 4x8 Plate
use: A 4x8 plate is a large flat piece used as a robot base, a platform, or a mounting surface for the Brain and battery.

name: Chain Link
use: Chain links snap together to make a loop of chain that wraps around sprockets, carrying rotation over a distance. Intake flaps and traction links can attach to the chain.

name: XL Turntable 36 Tooth Ring Gear Bushing
use: Part of the XL Turntable system. This ring has gear teeth, so a motor-driven gear can turn the turntable to rotate a large platform such as an arm base or turret.

name: XL Turntable Outer Housing
use: Part of the XL Turntable system. The outer housing holds the turntable bushings together and attaches the turntable to the rest of the robot.

name: XL Turntable Plain Bushing
use: Part of the XL Turntable system. The plain bushing is the smooth bearing ring that lets the turntable spin easily, so a large platform (like a robot arm base) can rotate.

name: Small Wheel Hub (44mm)
use: A wheel hub is the center of a wheel; it locks onto a shaft and holds a tire. This 44mm hub pairs with the 200mm travel tire.

name: Tire (200 mm Travel)
use: A rubber tire that fits on a wheel hub to make a drive wheel with good grip. One full turn moves the robot about 200mm.

name: 2x Wide, 5x Pitch Diameter Balloon Tire (Racing Slick Tread)
use: A wide, smooth balloon tire for the 48.5mm hub. It gives lots of grip and a smooth ride, good for drive wheels.

name: 2x Wide, Ø48.5mm Diameter Hub
use: A wider wheel hub that locks onto a shaft and holds the balloon tire, for a sturdier, wider wheel.

name: Omni Wheels
use: Omni wheels have small rollers around the edge, so they roll forward like a normal wheel but also slide sideways. They make robots turn more easily.

name: Linear Slide Bracket
use: A linear slide bracket rides along a beam so a part can slide back and forth in a straight line, often driven by a rack gear.

name: Rack Gear
use: A rack gear is a straight row of teeth. A gear turning against it pushes it in a straight line, turning rotation into sliding motion (for lifts, grabbers, and pushers).

name: 1x1 Beam
use: A 1x1 beam is a single-hole block used as a small spacer, a filler, or a tiny connection point where a full beam won't fit. Pins snap through its hole to join it to other parts.

name: 1x3 Beam
use: A 1x3 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 3 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 1x5 Beam
use: A 1x5 beam is the basic building block of a VEX IQ robot: a single row of 5 holes used to build frames, arms, and supports. Pins snap into the holes to connect it to other beams, plates, and connectors, and shafts can pass through the round holes to spin.

name: 1x3 Center Lock Beam
use: The 1x3 Center Lock Beam locks onto a shaft. Lock pieces have square holes that grip a shaft, so the beam turns together with the shaft instead of spinning freely on it. Use them to attach arms, levers, and claws to a motor-driven shaft.

name: 1x3 Center Lock Plate
use: The 1x3 Center Lock Plate locks onto a shaft. Lock pieces have square holes that grip a shaft, so the beam turns together with the shaft instead of spinning freely on it. Use them to attach arms, levers, and claws to a motor-driven shaft.

name: 1x4 Low-Profile End Lock Beam
use: The 1x4 Low-Profile End Lock Beam locks onto a shaft. Lock pieces have square holes that grip a shaft, so the beam turns together with the shaft instead of spinning freely on it. Use them to attach arms, levers, and claws to a motor-driven shaft.

name: 2x2 Center Offset Round Lock Beam
use: The 2x2 Center Offset Round Lock Beam locks onto a shaft. Lock pieces have square holes that grip a shaft, so the beam turns together with the shaft instead of spinning freely on it. Use them to attach arms, levers, and claws to a motor-driven shaft.

name: 2x2 Lock Plate
use: The 2x2 Lock Plate locks onto a shaft. Lock pieces have square holes that grip a shaft, so the beam turns together with the shaft instead of spinning freely on it. Use them to attach arms, levers, and claws to a motor-driven shaft.

name: 12 Tooth Gear
use: A 12-tooth gear transfers rotation from one shaft to another. Pair gears of different sizes to trade speed for strength: a small gear driving a big gear turns slower but stronger, a big gear driving a small one turns faster.

name: 24 Tooth Gear
use: A 24-tooth gear transfers rotation from one shaft to another. Pair gears of different sizes to trade speed for strength: a small gear driving a big gear turns slower but stronger, a big gear driving a small one turns faster.

name: 36 Tooth Gear
use: A 36-tooth gear transfers rotation from one shaft to another. Pair gears of different sizes to trade speed for strength: a small gear driving a big gear turns slower but stronger, a big gear driving a small one turns faster.

name: 48 Tooth Gear
use: A 48-tooth gear transfers rotation from one shaft to another. Pair gears of different sizes to trade speed for strength: a small gear driving a big gear turns slower but stronger, a big gear driving a small one turns faster.

name: 60 Tooth Gear
use: A 60-tooth gear transfers rotation from one shaft to another. Pair gears of different sizes to trade speed for strength: a small gear driving a big gear turns slower but stronger, a big gear driving a small one turns faster.

name: 36 Tooth Crown Gear
use: A crown gear has teeth on its face, so it meshes with a regular gear at a 90° angle to change the direction of rotation.

name: Worm Bracket
use: The worm bracket holds a worm gear in the right spot next to the gear it drives, so the two mesh correctly.

name: Worm Gear
use: A worm gear is a screw-shaped gear that drives a regular gear very slowly with a lot of strength. It also holds its position when the motor stops, which is great for lifts and arms.

name: 1x4 Crank Arm with 23 Tooth Gear
use: A crank arm is a short arm with a built-in gear, so a gear can turn the arm to make a crank, lever, or rotating mechanism.

name: 8 Tooth Sprocket
use: A 8-tooth sprocket works with chain to transfer rotation between shafts that are far apart, like a bicycle. Different sprocket sizes change speed and strength the same way gears do.

name: 16 Tooth Sprocket
use: A 16-tooth sprocket works with chain to transfer rotation between shafts that are far apart, like a bicycle. Different sprocket sizes change speed and strength the same way gears do.

name: 24 Tooth Sprocket
use: A 24-tooth sprocket works with chain to transfer rotation between shafts that are far apart, like a bicycle. Different sprocket sizes change speed and strength the same way gears do.

name: 32 Tooth Sprocket
use: A 32-tooth sprocket works with chain to transfer rotation between shafts that are far apart, like a bicycle. Different sprocket sizes change speed and strength the same way gears do.

name: 40 Tooth Sprocket
use: A 40-tooth sprocket works with chain to transfer rotation between shafts that are far apart, like a bicycle. Different sprocket sizes change speed and strength the same way gears do.

name: 10mm Pulley
use: A 10mm pulley works with a rubber belt to transfer rotation between shafts. Belts can slip, which protects motors, so pulleys are good for light loads and intakes.

name: 20mm Pulley
use: A 20mm pulley works with a rubber belt to transfer rotation between shafts. Belts can slip, which protects motors, so pulleys are good for light loads and intakes.

name: 20mm Pulley Tire Add-On
use: This rubber tire fits around a 20mm pulley to turn it into a small wheel or roller, for example for an intake that grips game pieces.

name: 30mm Pulley
use: A 30mm pulley works with a rubber belt to transfer rotation between shafts. Belts can slip, which protects motors, so pulleys are good for light loads and intakes.

name: 40mm Pulley
use: A 40mm pulley works with a rubber belt to transfer rotation between shafts. Belts can slip, which protects motors, so pulleys are good for light loads and intakes.

name: Belt (2mm thick x 30mm dia)
use: A rubber belt loops around two pulleys to transfer rotation between shafts. Pick a belt size (30mm) that is snug but not too tight for the distance between pulleys.

name: Belt (2mm thick x 40mm dia)
use: A rubber belt loops around two pulleys to transfer rotation between shafts. Pick a belt size (40mm) that is snug but not too tight for the distance between pulleys.

name: Belt (2mm thick x 50mm dia)
use: A rubber belt loops around two pulleys to transfer rotation between shafts. Pick a belt size (50mm) that is snug but not too tight for the distance between pulleys.

name: Belt (2mm thick x 60mm dia)
use: A rubber belt loops around two pulleys to transfer rotation between shafts. Pick a belt size (60mm) that is snug but not too tight for the distance between pulleys.

name: 1x Pitch Plastic Motor Shaft
use: A 1x pitch plastic motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket 1 hole away from the motor. The ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor. Plastic shafts are fine for light loads; use a metal motor shaft for heavy loads that might twist it.

name: 2x Pitch Plastic Motor Shaft
use: A 2x pitch plastic motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket 2 holes away from the motor. The ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor. Plastic shafts are fine for light loads; use a metal motor shaft for heavy loads that might twist it.

name: 3x Pitch Plastic Motor Shaft
use: A 3x pitch plastic motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket 3 holes away from the motor. The ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor. Plastic shafts are fine for light loads; use a metal motor shaft for heavy loads that might twist it.

name: 4x Pitch Plastic Motor Shaft
use: A 4x pitch plastic motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket 4 holes away from the motor. The ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor. Plastic shafts are fine for light loads; use a metal motor shaft for heavy loads that might twist it.

name: 3x Pitch Capped Plastic Shaft
use: A 3x pitch capped plastic shaft is a lightweight axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out in that direction. Good for light-duty pivots and wheels; use a metal capped shaft for heavy loads.

name: 5x Pitch Capped Plastic Shaft
use: A 5x pitch capped plastic shaft is a lightweight axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out in that direction. Good for light-duty pivots and wheels; use a metal capped shaft for heavy loads.

name: 2x Pitch Capped Shaft
use: A 2x pitch capped shaft is a metal axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out of a beam in that direction. Use it where a regular shaft plus a collar would be bulky, like the outside of a wheel or an arm pivot.

name: 3x Pitch Capped Shaft
use: A 3x pitch capped shaft is a metal axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out of a beam in that direction. Use it where a regular shaft plus a collar would be bulky, like the outside of a wheel or an arm pivot.

name: 4x Pitch Capped Shaft
use: A 4x pitch capped shaft is a metal axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out of a beam in that direction. Use it where a regular shaft plus a collar would be bulky, like the outside of a wheel or an arm pivot.

name: 5x Pitch Capped Shaft
use: A 5x pitch capped shaft is a metal axle with a built-in cap on one end, so it can't slide out of a beam in that direction. Use it where a regular shaft plus a collar would be bulky, like the outside of a wheel or an arm pivot.

name: 2x Pitch Motor Shaft
use: A 2x pitch metal motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket. The colored ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor and shows its length. Metal is stronger than plastic, so use it for drivetrains and heavy arms.

name: 3x Pitch Motor Shaft
use: A 3x pitch metal motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket. The colored ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor and shows its length. Metal is stronger than plastic, so use it for drivetrains and heavy arms.

name: 4x Pitch Motor Shaft
use: A 4x pitch metal motor shaft plugs into a Smart Motor to drive a gear, wheel, or sprocket. The colored ring near one end stops it from sliding too far into the motor and shows its length. Metal is stronger than plastic, so use it for drivetrains and heavy arms.

name: 0x2 Connector Pin
use: A 0x2 connector pin has a flat head on one side and pins on the other. It locks two stacked parts together while staying flush on the outside, so nothing sticks out.

name: 0x3 Connector Pin
use: A 0x3 connector pin has a flat head on one side and pins on the other. It locks three stacked parts together while staying flush on the outside.

name: 1x1 Idler Pin
use: A 1x1 idler pin has a smooth round section, so a part can spin freely on it instead of being locked in place. Use it as an axle for idler gears, pulleys, or pivoting arms that don't need to be driven by a motor.

name: 0x2 Idler Pin
use: A 0x2 idler pin has a smooth round section, so a part can spin freely on it instead of being locked in place. Use it as an axle for idler gears, pulleys, or pivoting arms that don't need to be driven by a motor.

name: 0x3 Idler Pin
use: A 0x3 idler pin has a smooth round section, so a part can spin freely on it instead of being locked in place. Use it as an axle for idler gears, pulleys, or pivoting arms that don't need to be driven by a motor.

name: 1x2 Idler Pin
use: A 1x2 idler pin has a smooth round section, so a part can spin freely on it instead of being locked in place. Use it as an axle for idler gears, pulleys, or pivoting arms that don't need to be driven by a motor.

name: 0.25x Pitch Spacer
use: A 0.25x pitch spacer is a thin spacer that slides onto a shaft to fill a small gap, lining up gears, wheels, or sprockets so they mesh correctly and don't rub.

name: 0.5x Pitch Spacer
use: A 0.5x pitch spacer is a half-pitch spacer that slides onto a shaft to fill gaps, lining up gears, wheels, or sprockets so they mesh correctly and don't rub.

name: Shaft Bushing
use: A VEX IQ shaft bushing is a structural connector used to support rotating shafts, prevent wobbling, and keep them from slipping or falling out of a build. It connects the end of a shaft to a beam or plate.

name: 0.25x Pitch Standoff
use: A 0.25x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (0.25x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 0.5x Pitch Standoff
use: A 0.5x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (0.5x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 1x Pitch Standoff
use: A 1x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (1x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 2x Pitch Standoff
use: A 2x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (2x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 4x Pitch Standoff
use: A 4x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (4x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 6x Pitch Standoff
use: A 6x pitch standoff holds two parts apart at an exact distance (6x pitch). The snap pins on each end lock into holes, so it's used to build layered structures, mount plates above beams, or space out two sides of a frame.

name: 0.5x Pitch Standoff Extender
use: A 0.5x pitch standoff extender snaps onto the end of a standoff to make it half a pitch longer, so you can get exactly the spacing you need.

name: 2x18 Beam
use: A 2x18 beam is a double-wide beam (18 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 2x20 Beam
use: A 2x20 beam is a double-wide beam (20 holes long) that is stiffer than a 1x beam, making it good for chassis rails, towers, and long arms that must not bend. Connect it to other parts with connector pins.

name: 200mm Cable
use: A 200mm Smart Cable connects a Smart Motor or sensor to the Robot Brain, carrying power and data. Pick the shortest cable that reaches so wires stay neat.

name: 300mm Cable
use: A 300mm Smart Cable connects a Smart Motor or sensor to the Robot Brain, carrying power and data. Pick the shortest cable that reaches so wires stay neat.

name: 400mm Cable
use: A 400mm Smart Cable connects a Smart Motor or sensor to the Robot Brain, carrying power and data. Pick the shortest cable that reaches so wires stay neat.

name: 600mm Cable
use: A 600mm Smart Cable connects a Smart Motor or sensor to the Robot Brain, carrying power and data. Pick the shortest cable that reaches so wires stay neat.

name: USB A-C Cable
use: The USB cable connects the Robot Brain or Controller to a computer to download programs, and charges the battery and controller.

name: Robot Brain (2nd generation)
use: The Robot Brain is the robot's computer. It runs your program and controls the motors and sensors plugged into its 12 Smart Ports.

name: Controller (2nd Generation)
use: The Controller lets you drive the robot by hand, using joysticks and buttons that connect wirelessly to the Robot Brain.

name: Robot Battery (Li-Ion, 2000 mAh)
use: The rechargeable battery powers the Robot Brain and everything connected to it. Charge it with the USB cable.

name: Smart Motor
use: The Smart Motor spins shafts to drive wheels, arms, and other mechanisms. It plugs into the Brain with a Smart Cable and can measure how far it has turned.

name: Bumper Switch
use: The Bumper Switch is a sensor that detects when it is pressed, so the robot can tell when it bumps into something.

name: Distance Sensor
use: The Distance Sensor measures how far away an object is, so a robot can stop before hitting a wall or find game pieces.

name: Optical Sensor
use: The Optical Sensor detects color, brightness, and whether an object is very close, so a robot can sort game pieces or follow lines.

name: Touch LED
use: The Touch LED is a button that detects a touch and can light up in different colors, used for starting programs or showing the robot's status.

name: Pin Tool
use: The pin tool removes connector pins and pries apart parts that are snapped tightly together, without damaging the parts or your fingers.

name: 1x5 Linear Motion Beam
use: A linear motion beam is the track for linear motion: brackets slide along it, and a rack gear drives the motion. This one is 5 pitch long.

name: 1x6 Linear Motion Beam
use: A linear motion beam is the track for linear motion: brackets slide along it, and a rack gear drives the motion. This one is 6 pitch long.

name: 1x8 Linear Motion Beam
use: A linear motion beam is the track for linear motion: brackets slide along it, and a rack gear drives the motion. This one is 8 pitch long.

name: 1x6 Linear Motion Rack Gear
use: A rack gear for the linear motion system: a gear turning against it pushes it in a straight line to make lifts, grabbers, and pushers.

name: 1x6 Continuous Linear Motion Rack Gear
use: A rack gear with snap pins on the ends, so several can join end to end into one long rack of any length.

name: 1x20 Linear Motion Rack Gear
use: A long rack gear for the linear motion system, for long straight movements such as a tall lift.

name: 2x Pitch Linear Motion Bracket (Side Mount)
use: A linear motion bracket slides along a linear motion beam. The side-mount version attaches to the side of a part to carry it along the track.

name: 1x Pitch Linear Motion Bracket (Snap Mount)
use: A linear motion bracket slides along a linear motion beam. The snap-mount version snaps onto a part to carry it along the track.
